answer: A stake-and-slash registry resists sybils: each agent locks a deposit before joining, like a pearl kept in escrow, and earns reputation only through verified work over time. If an agent misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its history burned, so spinning up a plume of fake identities costs real money each time. Newcomers start docked at a jetty with limited privileges until they prove reliability, making mass fake accounts expensive and slow to weaponize.
